Unit of an object's own measure

Source: R/units.R
getUnit.Rd

The one quantity an object measures itself in, as opposed to the table of parameter units getUnits() reports: the commodity a flow is counted in for commodity, demand, import, export, supply and trade, and the value of the series for weather.

Usage

getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'commodity'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'demand'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'import'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'export'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'supply'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'weather'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'technology'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'storage'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'trade'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'tax'
getUnit(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'subsidy'
getUnit(object, ...)

Arguments

object

an object with a @units slot.

...

not used.

Value

A single character value, or NA_character_ when the object declares no unit.

Details

It is stored in @units – the comm column, or wval for weather – and set with the unit = argument of the constructors. Up to version 0.91 it was a slot of its own, @unit; that slot is gone, and this accessor replaces every read of it.

Examples

getUnit(newCommodity(name = "ELC", desc = "Electricity", unit = "GWh"))
#> [1] "GWh"
getUnit(newCommodity(name = "ELC"))
#> [1] NA
